claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is single-phase BCC and dendritic.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 800 MPa at lower temperatures.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding a controlled nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion will stabilize the TiVNbTa microstructure at 1273 K.
The intervention will produce nanoscale, uniformly distributed Y2O3 particles embedded in the dendritic matrix.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will pin or impede dislocations at elevated temperature.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
The oxide dispersion will reduce microstructural recovery and creep.
Reduced dislocation motion, grain-boundary sliding, recovery, and creep will maintain higher yield and compressive strength at 1273 K.
The oxide-dispersion-modified alloy will have a yield strength above the 330 MPa baseline at 1273 K.
The modified alloy's yield strength at 1273 K may approach or exceed 500 MPa.
The modification will improve compressive strength and ductility retention at 1273 K.
The intervention is applicable near 1273 K under steady-state heat transfer and cyclic thermomechanical loading between W and CuCrZr.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on Y2O3 concentration, particle size and distribution, and processing parameters.
The oxide dispersion may adversely affect thermal conductivity.
